course_description:
Students gain hands-on skills in writing, editing, and designing effective promotional publications and creating/producing strategic materials. In this rich immersion experience, students produce work within traditional and new media environments, for a real client.

This course introduces you to the art and practice of strategic communication writing. You’ll learn how to pitch stories that capture journalists’ attention, how to write content that doesn’t just inform but genuinely engages, and how to tailor messages for different audiences and media environments. From planning and message development to understanding key genres of strategic communication, the course shows you how to transform ideas into compelling pieces of communication that get noticed.

course_aims: This course aims to build on your understanding of public relations practice which is developed in COMU1052. You will learn the techniques of content creation for both traditional and new media, and the strategic deployment of collateral in public relations practice across a range of collaterals for a real client.

learning_outcomes.description: Analyse the rapidly changing context for the composition and dissemination of strategic communication material, and how this shapes organisational reputation.
Become familiar with using different forms of strategic communication writing, the range of strategic communication writing tools used in practice, and the adaptation of tools for cross-platform use.
Critically assess the effectiveness of strategic communication writing with a focus on the usefulness of AI prompts and reflection.
Undertake effective reviewing, revising and editing of strategic communication writing with and without the use of artificial intelligence tools.
Apply strategic writing principles including clarity, conciseness, consistency, coherence, creativity and use of plain language.
Demonstrate an ability for connecting with target audiences using strong professional writing skills for various forms of strategic communication writing.
Learn to design and produce a range of strategic communication collaterals to suit an organisation's needs.
Understand the ethical and legal standards of practice in the composition of strategic communication material, including through the use of AI tools.

As a UQ student, you must comply with University-wide and program-specific requirements, including the: Student Code of Conduct Policy Student Integrity and Misconduct Policy and Procedure Assessment Procedure Examinations Procedure Reasonable Adjustments for Students Policy and Procedure AI for Assessment Guide Recording of Teaching Policy and Procedure Learn more about UQ policies on my.UQ and the Policy and Procedure Library . Course guidelines Communication Expectations While you are a student at UQ, all communication must be conducted according to the UQ Student Code of Conduct . The UQ Library has a helpful Communicate and collaborate online module . Email is the primary way for you to send messages to, and receive information from, the School and our staff. You must use your UQ email address (not a private address) to communicate with staff. You should add a clear subject line, including course code, and a 2-3 word statement. You can send email at any time, however, please do not expect responses outside normal working hours (Monday to Friday from ~8am to ~5pm). Emails that constitute bullying, harassment or discrimination against staff contravene the Student Code of Conduct. Emails like this will be reported to the University, and the matter will be pursued as misconduct. Learning activities
